amendments.name: Amendment a

code.decode: Inconsistency And/or Error In The Protocol

amendments.summary: For consistency with prior mirikizumab studies, the inclusion criteria [12b] is updated with the following maximum baseline liver enzyme levels: alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and aspartate aminotransferase (AST) ≤2 x ULN, alkaline phosphatase (ALP) ≤1.5 x ULN, and total bilirubin level (TBL) ≤1.5 x ULN. To specify that any participant who experiences serious or severe GI AEs that are consistent with worsening of UC and do not improve with the recommendations for management of intolerable GI symptoms related to tirzepatide will be evaluated for UC disease worsening. To clarify that every symptom-directed examination will also include an examination of the heart, lungs, abdomen, neurological system, thyroid, and visual examination of the skin, consistent with the existing text in the schedule of activities under "Complete Physical Examination." To add acute kidney injury as an AESI to the protocol. To include pregnancy testing every 4 weeks. This can include home urine pregnancy testing. To update that follow-up information for pregnancy outcomes for participant and neonate will be collected until termination of the pregnancy or for at least 12 months post-delivery.

amendments.name: Amendment e

code.decode: Inconsistency And/or Error In The Protocol

amendments.summary: This amendment is considered to be substantial because it is likely to have a significant impact on the safety or the rights of the study participants. Changes include: replacement of "mucosal healing" with "histologic-endoscopic mucosal improvement plus absence of neutrophils" per regulatory feedback; clarification of lifestyle goals in the Schedule of Activities; correction of hematology and clinical chemistry testing for Visit 7; deletion of mMS review at Visits 8, 15, and ED; addition of risk assessment for gallbladder disease in tirzepatide; correction of exploratory endpoint for visceral fat measurement; addition of colorectal cancer surveillance wording to inclusion criteria; removal of duplicate text from inclusion criteria; clarifications to exclusion criteria; addition of ECG exclusion criterion per regulatory feedback; additional details for continued access to study interventions; and correction of FDA guidance reference year.

arms.name: Mirikizumab + Tirzepatide
arms.description: Participants receive mirikizumab (300 mg IV at Weeks 0, 4, 8 for induction; 200 mg SC Q4W from Week 12 for maintenance) concomitantly with tirzepatide subcutaneous injection with dose escalation from 2.5 mg QW up to maximum tolerated dose (MTD) of up to 15 mg QW

arms.name: Mirikizumab + Placebo
arms.description: Participants receive mirikizumab (300 mg IV at Weeks 0, 4, 8 for induction; 200 mg SC Q4W from Week 12 for maintenance) concomitantly with placebo to match tirzepatide subcutaneous injection administered weekly

objectives.name: Primary Efficacy Objective
objectives.text: To evaluate if concomitant administration of mirikizumab and tirzepatide at the MTD (up to 15 mg) is superior to mirikizumab and placebo in simultaneously achieving clinical remission and weight reduction

endpoints.name: Primary Endpoint: Simultaneous Clinical Remission and Weight Reduction at Week 52
endpoints.text: Proportion of participants who simultaneously achieve clinical remission and at least 10% weight reduction at Week 52

objectives.name: Key Secondary Gastroenterologic Outcomes Objective

intercurrentEvents.name: Permanent discontinuation of study intervention (Primary Estimand: Simultaneous Clinical Remission and At Least 10% Weight Reduction at Week 52)

Patients with UC should undergo colorectal cancer surveillance starting at 8 years after disease onset, as they are at higher risk of developing colorectal cancer. This timing allows for optimal prevention and early detection of colorectal cancer or dysplasia.

Clinical remission, as defined in Section 8.1, was chosen based on regulatory guidance from FDA (2016) and EMA (2018). Both recommend a composite endpoint for both symptomatic and endoscopic remission.

A body weight reduction of at least 5% is considered the threshold for clinically meaningful effect on the basis of improvement in metabolic health. Greater weight reductions yield additional clinical benefits and may be required for improvement in certain weight-related conditions.

studyInterventions.name: Mirikizumab
studyInterventions.description: Humanized IgG4_variant monoclonal antibody that binds to the p19 subunit of IL_23; administered IV during induction and SC during maintenance for moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis

studyInterventions.name: Tirzepatide
studyInterventions.description: GIP receptor and GLP_1 receptor agonist administered SC QW with dose escalation up to MTD of 15 mg; co_administered with mirikizumab in the active treatment arm

studyInterventions.name: Placebo to match tirzepatide
studyInterventions.description: Subcutaneous placebo matching tirzepatide, administered QW in the mirikizumab + placebo control arm

studyInterventions.name: Oral corticosteroids
studyInterventions.description: Permitted at stable dose prior to screening colonoscopy; subject to taper per Section 6.9.5

studyInterventions.name: Antihyperglycemic medications
studyInterventions.description: Concomitant antihyperglycemic medications permitted per Section 6.9.2 with dose stabilization requirements

studyInterventions.name: IV corticosteroids
studyInterventions.description: Prohibited within 2 weeks prior to screening colonoscopy and throughout screening (Exclusion Criterion 50)
